controls.NIST:ID.AM-1: Physical devices and systems within the organization are inventoried
controls.NIST:ID.AM-2: Software platforms and applications within the organization are inventoried
controls.NIST:ID.AM-3: Organizational communication and data flows are mapped
controls.NIST:ID.AM-5: Resources (e.g., hardware, devices, data, time, personnel, and software) are prioritized based on their classification, criticality, and business value
controls.NIST:ID.AM-6: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for the entire workforce and third-party stakeholders (e.g., suppliers, customers, partners) are established
controls.NIST:ID.BE-1: The organization’s role in the supply chain is identified and communicated
controls.NIST:ID.BE-2: The organization’s place in critical infrastructure and its industry sector is identified and communicated
controls.NIST:ID.BE-3: Priorities for organizational mission, objectives, and activities are established and communicated
controls.NIST:ID.BE-4: Dependencies and critical functions for delivery of critical services are established
controls.NIST:ID.BE-5: Resilience requirements to support delivery of critical services are established for all operating states (e.g. under duress/attack, during recovery, normal operations)
controls.NIST:ID.GV-1: Organizational cybersecurity policy is established and communicated
controls.NIST:ID.GV-2: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities are coordinated and aligned with internal roles and external partners
controls.NIST:ID.GV-3: Legal and regulatory requirements regarding cybersecurity, including privacy and civil liberties obligations, are understood and managed
controls.NIST:ID.GV-4: Governance and risk management processes address cybersecurity risks
controls.NIST:ID.RA-1: Asset vulnerabilities are identified and documented
controls.NIST:ID.RA-2: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
controls.NIST:ID.RA-3: Threats, both internal and external, are identified and documented
controls.NIST:ID.RA-4: Potential business impacts and likelihoods are identified
controls.NIST:ID.RA-5: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to determine risk
controls.NIST:ID.RA-6: Risk responses are identified and prioritized
controls.NIST:ID.RM-1: Risk management processes are established, managed, and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
controls.NIST:ID.RM-2: Organizational risk tolerance is determined and clearly expressed
controls.NIST:ID.RM-3: The organization’s determination of risk tolerance is informed by its role in critical infrastructure and sector specific risk analysis
controls.NIST:ID.SC-1: Cyber supply chain risk management processes are identified, established, assessed, managed, and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
controls.NIST:ID.SC-2: Suppliers and third party partners of information systems, components, and services are identified, prioritized, and assessed using a cyber supply chain risk assessment process
controls.NIST:ID.SC-3: Contracts with suppliers and third-party partners are used to implement appropriate measures designed to meet the objectives of an organization’s cybersecurity program and Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management Plan.
controls.NIST:ID.SC-4: Suppliers and third-party partners are routinely assessed using audits, test results, or other forms of evaluations to confirm they are meeting their contractual obligations.
controls.NIST:ID.SC-5: Response and recovery planning and testing are conducted with suppliers and third-party providers
controls.NIST:PR.AC-1: Identities and credentials are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited for authorized devices, users and processes
controls.NIST:PR.AC-2: Physical access to assets is managed and protected
controls.NIST:PR.AC-4: Access permissions and authorizations are managed, incorporating the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
controls.NIST:PR.AC-5: Network integrity is protected (e.g., network segregation, network segmentation)
controls.NIST:PR.AC-6: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials and asserted in interactions
controls.NIST:PR.AC-7: Users, devices, and other assets are authenticated (e.g., single-factor, multi-factor) commensurate with the risk of the transaction (e.g., individuals’ security and privacy risks and other organizational risks)
controls.NIST:PR.AT-1: All users are informed and trained
controls.NIST:PR.AT-2: Privileged users understand their roles and responsibilities
controls.NIST:PR.AT-3: Third-party stakeholders (e.g., suppliers, customers, partners) understand their roles and responsibilities
controls.NIST:PR.AT-4: Senior executives understand their roles and responsibilities
controls.NIST:PR.AT-5: Physical and cybersecurity personnel understand their roles and responsibilities
controls.NIST:PR.DS-3: Assets are formally managed throughout removal, transfers, and disposition
controls.NIST:PR.DS-4: Adequate capacity to ensure availability is maintained
controls.NIST:PR.DS-5: Protections against data leaks are implemented
controls.NIST:PR.DS-6: Integrity checking mechanisms are used to verify software, firmware, and information integrity
controls.NIST:PR.DS-7: The development and testing environment(s) are separate from the production environment
controls.NIST:PR.DS-8: Integrity checking mechanisms are used to verify hardware integrity
controls.NIST:PR.IP-1: A baseline configuration of information technology/industrial control systems is created and maintained incorporating security principles (e.g. concept of least functionality)
controls.NIST:PR.IP-2: A System Development Life Cycle to manage systems is implemented
controls.NIST:PR.IP-3: Configuration change control processes are in place
controls.NIST:PR.IP-4: Backups of information are conducted, maintained, and tested
controls.NIST:PR.IP-5: Policy and regulations regarding the physical operating environment for organizational assets are met
controls.NIST:PR.IP-6: Data is destroyed according to policy
controls.NIST:PR.IP-8: Effectiveness of protection technologies is shared
controls.NIST:PR.IP-9: Response plans (Incident Response and Business Continuity) and recovery plans (Incident Recovery and Disaster Recovery) are in place and managed
controls.NIST:PR.IP-10: Response and recovery plans are tested
controls.NIST:PR.IP-11: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices (e.g., deprovisioning, personnel screening)
controls.NIST:PR.IP-12: A vulnerability management plan is developed and implemented
controls.NIST:PR.MA-1: Maintenance and repair of organizational assets are performed and logged, with approved and controlled tools
controls.NIST:PR.MA-2: Remote maintenance of organizational assets is approved, logged, and performed in a manner that prevents unauthorized access
controls.NIST:PR.PT-1: Audit/log records are determined, documented, implemented, and reviewed in accordance with policy
controls.NIST:PR.PT-2: Removable media is protected and its use restricted according to policy
controls.NIST:PR.PT-3: The principle of least functionality is incorporated by configuring systems to provide only essential capabilities
controls.NIST:PR.PT-4: Communications and control networks are protected
controls.NIST:PR.PT-5: Mechanisms (e.g., failsafe, load balancing, hot swap) are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations
controls.NIST:DE.AE-1: A baseline of network operations and expected data flows for users and systems is established and managed
controls.NIST:DE.AE-2: Detected events are analyzed to understand attack targets and methods
controls.NIST:DE.AE-3: Event data are collected and correlated from multiple sources and sensors
controls.NIST:DE.CM-1: The network is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events
controls.NIST:DE.CM-2: The physical environment is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events
controls.NIST:DE.CM-3: Personnel activity is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events
controls.NIST:DE.CM-6: External service provider activity is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events
controls.NIST:DE.CM-7: Monitoring for unauthorized personnel, connections, devices, and software is performed
controls.NIST:DE.DP-1: Roles and responsibilities for detection are well defined to ensure accountability
controls.NIST:DE.DP-2: Detection activities comply with all applicable requirements
controls.NIST:RS.RP-1: Response plan is executed during or after an incident
controls.NIST:RS.CO-1: Personnel know their roles and order of operations when a response is needed
controls.NIST:RS.CO-2: Incidents are reported consistent with established criteria
controls.NIST:RS.CO-3: Information is shared consistent with response plans
controls.NIST:RS.CO-4: Coordination with stakeholders occurs consistent with response plans
controls.NIST:RS.CO-5: Voluntary information sharing occurs with external stakeholders to achieve broader cybersecurity situational awareness
controls.NIST:RS.AN-1: Notifications from detection systems are investigated
controls.NIST:RS.AN-2: The impact of the incident is understood
controls.NIST:RS.AN-4: Incidents are categorized consistent with response plans
controls.NIST:RS.AN-5: Processes are established to receive, analyze and respond to vulnerabilities disclosed to the organization from internal and external sources (e.g. internal testing, security bulletins, or security researchers)
controls.NIST:RS.MI-3: Newly identified vulnerabilities are mitigated or documented as accepted risks
controls.NIST:RC.RP-1: Recovery plan is executed during or after a cybersecurity incident
controls.NIST:RC.CO-2: Reputation is repaired after an incident
controls.NIST:RC.CO-3: Recovery activities are communicated to internal and external stakeholders as well as executive and management teams

controls.ISM_O:0418: Credentials are kept separate from systems they are used to authenticate to, except for when performing authentication activities.
controls.ISM_O:0421: Passphrases used for single-factor authentication are at least 4 random words with a total minimum length of 14 characters, unless more stringent requirements apply.
controls.ISM_O:0422: Passphrases used for single-factor authentication on TOP SECRET systems are at least 6 random words with a total minimum length of 20 characters.
controls.ISM_O:0846: All users (with the exception of local administrator accounts and break glass accounts) cannot disable, bypass or be exempted from application control.
controls.ISM_O:0974: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate unprivileged users of systems.
controls.ISM_O:0988: An accurate time source is established and used consistently across systems to assist with identifying connections between events.
controls.ISM_O:1034: A HIPS is implemented on critical servers and high-value servers.
controls.ISM_O:1055: LAN Manager and NT LAN Manager authentication methods are disabled.
controls.ISM_O:1173: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate privileged users of systems.
controls.ISM_O:1277: Data communicated between database servers and web servers is encrypted.
controls.ISM_O:1288: Files imported or exported via gateways or CDSs undergo antivirus scanning using multiple different scanning engines.
controls.ISM_O:1311: SNMP version 1 and SNMP version 2 are not used on networks.
controls.ISM_O:1315: The administrative interface on wireless access points is disabled for wireless network connections.
controls.ISM_O:1319: Static addressing is not used for assigning IP addresses on wireless networks.
controls.ISM_O:1341: A HIPS is implemented on workstations.
controls.ISM_O:1386: Network management traffic can only originate from administrative infrastructure.
controls.ISM_O:1401: Multi-factor authentication uses either: something users have and something users know, or something users have that is unlocked by something users know or are.
controls.ISM_O:1402: Credentials stored on systems are protected by a password manager; a hardware security module; or by salting, hashing and stretching them before storage within a database
controls.ISM_O:1405: A centralised event logging facility is implemented and event logs are sent to the facility as soon as possible after they occur.
controls.ISM_O:1409: Operating systems are hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur
controls.ISM_O:1416: A software firewall is implemented on workstations and servers to restrict inbound and outbound network connections to an organisation-approved set of applications and services.
controls.ISM_O:1417: Antivirus software is implemented on workstations and server.
controls.ISM_O:1418: If there is no business requirement for reading from removable media and devices, such functionality is disabled via the use of device access control software or by disabling external communication interfaces
controls.ISM_O:1446: When using elliptic curve cryptography, a suitable curve from NIST SP 800-186 is used.
controls.ISM_O:1449: SSH private keys are protected with a passphrase or a key encryption key
controls.ISM_O:1467: The latest release of office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF software, and security products are used.
controls.ISM_O:1483: The latest release of internet-facing server applications are used.
controls.ISM_O:1491: Unprivileged users are prevented from running script execution engines.
controls.ISM_O:1493: Software registers for workstations, servers, network devices and other ICT equipment are developed, implemented, maintained and verified on a regular basis.
controls.ISM_O:1504: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users to their organisation’s online services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive data.
controls.ISM_O:1505: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users of data repositories.
controls.ISM_O:1506: The use of SSH version 1 is disabled for SSH connections.
controls.ISM_O:1546: Users are authenticated before they are granted access to a system and its resources
controls.ISM_O:1552: All web application content is offered exclusively using HTTPS.
controls.ISM_O:1557: Passphrases used for single-factor authentication on SECRET systems are at least 5 random words with a total minimum length of 17 characters.
controls.ISM_O:1558: Passphrases used for single-factor authentication are not a list of categorised words; do not form a real sentence in a natural language; and are not constructed from song lyrics, movies, literature or any other publicly available material.
controls.ISM_O:1559: Memorised secrets used for multi-factor authentication are a minimum of 6 characters, unless more stringent requirements apply.
controls.ISM_O:1560: Memorised secrets used for multi-factor authentication on SECRET systems are a minimum of 8 characters
controls.ISM_O:1561: Memorised secrets used for multi-factor authentication on TOP SECRET systems are a minimum of 10 characters.
controls.ISM_O:1745: Early Launch Antimalware, Secure Boot, Trusted Boot and Measured Boot functionality is enabled.

controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.1: 1.1 Establish and implement firewall and router configuration standards that include the following:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.1.1: 1.1.1 A formal process for approving and testing all network connections and changes to the firewall and router configurations
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.1.2: 1.1.2 Current network diagram that identifies all connections between the cardholder data environment and other networks, including any wireless networks
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.1.3: 1.1.3 Current diagram that shows all cardholder data flows across systems and networks
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.1.4: 1.1.4 Requirements for a firewall at each Internet connection and between any demilitarized zone (DMZ) and the internal network zone
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.1.5: 1.1.5 Description of groups, roles, and responsibilities for management of network components
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.1.6: 1.1.6 Documentation and business justification for use of all services, protocols, and ports allowed, including documentation of security features implemented for those protocols considered to be insecure.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.1.7: 1.1.7 Requirement to review firewall and router rule sets at least every six months
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.2: 1.2 Build firewall and router configurations that restrict connections between untrusted networks and any system components in the cardholder data environment.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.2.1: 1.2.1 Restrict inbound and outbound traffic to that which is necessary for the cardholder data environment, and specifically deny all other traffic.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.2.2: 1.2.2 Secure and synchronize router configuration files.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.2.3: 1.2.3 Install perimeter firewalls between all wireless networks and the cardholder data environment, and configure these firewalls to deny or, if traffic is necessary for business purposes, permit only authorized traffic between the wireless environment and the cardholder data environment.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.3: 1.3 Prohibit direct public access between the Internet and any system component in the cardholder data environment.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.3.1: 1.3.1 Implement a DMZ to limit inbound traffic to only system components that provide authorized publicly accessible services, protocols, and ports.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.3.2: 1.3.2 Limit inbound Internet traffic to IP addresses within the DMZ.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.3.3: 1.3.3 Implement anti-spoofing measures to detect and block forged source IP addresses from entering the network.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.3.4: 1.3.4 Do not allow unauthorized outbound traffic from the cardholder data environment to the Internet.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.3.5: 1.3.5 Permit only "established" connections into the network.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.3.6: 1.3.6 Place system components that store cardholder data (such as a database) in an internal network zone, segregated from the DMZ and other untrusted networks
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.3.7: 1.3.7 Do not disclose private IP addresses and routing information to unauthorized parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.4: 1.4 Install personal firewall software on any mobile and/or employee-owned devices that connect to the Internet when outside the network (for example, laptops used by employees), and which are also used to access the network.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-1.5: 1.5 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for managing firewalls are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.1: 2.1 Always change vendor-supplied defaults and remove or disable unnecessary default accounts before installing a system on the network.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.1.1: 2.1.1 For wireless environments connected to the cardholder data environment or transmitting cardholder data, change ALL wireless vendor defaults at installation, including but not limited to default wireless encryption keys, passwords, and SNMP community strings.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.2: 2.2 Develop configuration standards for all system components. Assure that these standards address all known security vulnerabilities and are consistent with industry-accepted system hardening standards.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.2.1: 2.2.1 Implement only one primary function per server to prevent functions that require different security levels from co-existing on the same server.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.2.2: 2.2.2 Enable only necessary services, protocols, daemons, etc., as required for the function of the system.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.2.3: 2.2.3 Implement additional security features for any required services, protocols, or daemons that are considered to be insecure
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.2.4: 2.2.4 Configure system security parameters to prevent misuse.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.2.5: 2.2.5 Remove all unnecessary functionality, such as scripts, drivers, features, subsystems, file systems, and unnecessary web servers.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.3: 2.3 Encrypt all non-console administrative access using strong cryptography. Use technologies such as SSH, VPN, or TLS for web-based management and other non-console administrative access.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.4: 2.4 Maintain an inventory of system components that are in scope for PCI DSS.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.5: 2.5 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for managing vendor defaults and other security parameters are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-2.6: 2.6 Shared hosting providers must protect each entity's hosted environment and cardholder data.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.1: 3.1 Keep cardholder data storage to a minimum by implementing data retention and disposal policies, procedures and processes that include at least the following for all cardholder data (CHD) storage:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.2: 3.2 Do not store sensitive authentication data after authorization (even if encrypted).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.2.1: 3.2.1 Do not store the full contents of any track (from the magnetic stripe located on the back of a card, equivalent data contained on a chip, or elsewhere) after authorization. This data is alternatively called full track, track, track 1, track 2, and magnetic- stripe data.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.2.2: 3.2.2 Do not store the card verification code or value (three-digit or four-digit number printed on the front or back of a payment card used to verify card-not- present transactions) after authorization.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.2.3: 3.2.3 Do not store the personal identification number (PIN) or the encrypted PIN block after authorization.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.3: 3.3 Mask PAN when displayed (the first six and last four digits are the maximum number of digits to be displayed), such that only personnel with a legitimate business need can see the full PAN.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.4: 3.4 Render PAN unreadable anywhere it is stored (including on portable digital media, backup media, and in logs) by using any of the following approaches:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.4.1: 3.4.1 If disk encryption is used (rather than file- or column-level database encryption), logical access must be managed separately and independently of native operating system authentication and access control mechanisms (for example, by not using local user account databases or general network login credentials). Decryption keys must not be associated with user accounts.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.5: 3.5 Document and implement procedures to protect keys used to secure stored cardholder data against disclosure and misuse:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.5.1: Additional requirement  for service  providers  only: Maintain a documented description of the cryptographic architecture that includes:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.5.2: 3.5.2 Restrict access to cryptographic keys to the fewest number of custodians necessary.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.5.3: 3.5.3 Store secret and private keys used to encrypt/decrypt cardholder data in one (or more) of the following forms at all times:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.5.4: 3.5.4 Store cryptographic keys in the fewest possible locations.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.6: 3.6 Fully document and implement all key-management processes and procedures for cryptographic keys used for encryption of cardholder data, including the following:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.6.4: 3.6.4 Cryptographic key changes for keys that have reached the end of their cryptoperiod (for example, after a defined period of time has passed and/or after a certain amount of cipher- text has been produced by a given key), as defined by the associated application vendor or key owner, and based on industry best practices and guidelines (for example, NIST Special Publication 800-57).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.6.5: 3.6.5 Retirement or replacement (for example, archiving, destruction, and/or revocation) of keys as deemed necessary when the integrity of the key has been weakened (for example, departure of an employee with knowledge of a clear-text key component), or keys are suspected of being compromised.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.6.6: 3.6.6 If manual clear-text cryptographic key-management operations are used, these operations must be managed using split knowledge and dual control.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.6.7: 3.6.7 Prevention of unauthorized substitution of cryptographic keys.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.6.8: 3.6.8 Requirement for cryptographic key custodians to formally acknowledge that they understand and accept their key-custodian responsibilities.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-3.7: 3.7 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for protecting stored cardholder data are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-4.1: 4.1 Use strong cryptography and security protocols (for example, TLS, IPSEC, SSH, etc.) to safeguard sensitive cardholder data during transmission over open, public networks, including the following:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-4.1.1: 4.1.1 Ensure wireless networks transmitting cardholder data or connected to the cardholder data environment, use industry best practices (for example, IEEE 802.11i) to implement strong encryption for authentication and transmission.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-4.2: 4.2 Never send unprotected PANs by end-user messaging technologies (for example, e-mail, instant messaging, SMS, chat, etc.).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-4.3: 4.3 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for encrypting transmissions of cardholder data are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-5.1: 5.1 Deploy anti-virus software on all systems commonly affected by malicious software (particularly personal computers and servers).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-5.1.1: 5.1.1 Ensure that anti-virus programs are capable of detecting, removing, and protecting against all known types of malicious software.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-5.1.2: 5.1.2 For systems considered to be not commonly affected by malicious software, perform periodic evaluations to identify and evaluate evolving malware threats in order to confirm whether such systems continue to not require anti-virus software.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-5.2: 5.2 Ensure that all anti-virus mechanisms are maintained as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-5.3: 5.3 Ensure that anti-virus mechanisms are actively running and cannot be disabled or altered by users, unless specifically authorized by management on a case-by-case basis for a limited time period.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-5.4: 5.4 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for protecting systems against malware are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.1: 6.1 Establish a process to identify security vulnerabilities, using reputable outside sources for security vulnerability information, and assign a risk ranking (for example, as 'high', 'medium', or 'low') to newly discovered security vulnerabilities.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.2: 6.2 Ensure that all system components and software are protected from known vulnerabilities by installing applicable vendor- supplied security patches. Install critical security patches within one month of release.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.3: 6.3 Develop internal and external software applications (including web-based administrative access to applications) securely, as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.3.1: 6.3.1 Remove development, test and/or custom application accounts, user IDs, and passwords before applications become active or are released to customers.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.3.2: 6.3.2 Review custom code prior to release to production or customers in order to identify any potential coding vulnerability (using either manual or automated processes) to include at least the following:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.4: 6.4 Follow change control processes and procedures for all changes to system components. The processes must include the following:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.4.1: 6.4.1 Separate development/test environments from production environments, and enforce the separation with access controls.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.4.2: 6.4.2 Separation of duties between development/test and production environments
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.4.3: 6.4.3 Production data (live PANs) are not used for testing or development
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.4.4: 6.4.4 Removal of test data and accounts before production systems become active
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.4.5: 6.4.5 Change control procedures for the implementation of security patches and software modifications must include the following:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.4.5.2: 6.4.5.2 Documented change approval by authorized parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.4.5.3: 6.4.5.3 Functionality testing to verify that the change does not adversely impact the security of the system.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.4.6: 6.4.6- Upon completion of a significant change, all relevant PCI DSS requirements must be implemented on all new or changed systems and networks, and documentation updated as applicable.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.5: 6.5 Address common coding vulnerabilities in software-development processes as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.5.1: 6.5.1 Injection flaws, particularly SQL injection. Also consider OS Command Injection, LDAP and XPath injection flaws as well as other injection flaws.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.5.6: 6.5.6 All "high risk" vulnerabilities identified in the vulnerability identification process (as defined in PCI DSS Requirement 6.1).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.5.8: 6.5.8 Improper access control (such as insecure direct object references, failure to restrict URL access, directory traversal, and failure to restrict user access to functions).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.6: 6.6 For public-facing web applications, address new threats and vulnerabilities on an ongoing basis and ensure these applications are protected against known attacks by either of the following methods:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-6.7: 6.7 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for developing and maintaining secure systems and applications are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-7.1: 7.1 Limit access to system components and cardholder data to only those individuals whose job requires such access.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-7.1.1: 7.1.1 Define access needs for each role, including:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-7.1.2: 7.1.2 Restrict access to privileged user IDs to least privileges necessary to perform job responsibilities.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-7.1.3: 7.1.3 Assign access based on individual personnel's job classification and function."
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-7.1.4: 7.1.4 Require documented approval by authorized parties specifying required privileges.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-7.2: 7.2 Establish an access control system for systems components that restricts access based on a user's need to know, and is set to 'deny all' unless specifically allowed.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-7.2.2: 7.2.2 Assignment of privileges to individuals based on job classification and function.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-7.3: 7.3 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for restricting access to cardholder data are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.1: 8.1 Define and implement policies and procedures to ensure proper user identification management for non-consumer users and administrators on all system components as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.1.1: 8.1.1 Assign all users a unique ID before allowing them to access system components or cardholder data.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.1.2: 8.1.2 Control addition, deletion, and modification of user IDs, credentials, and other identifier objects.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.1.3: 8.1.3 Immediately revoke access for any terminated users.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.1.4: 8.1.4 Remove/disable inactive user accounts within 90 days.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.1.5: 8.1.5 Manage IDs used by vendors to access, support, or maintain system components via remote access as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.1.6: 8.1.6 Limit repeated access attempts by locking out the user ID after not more than six attempts.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.1.7: 8.1.7 Set the lockout duration to a minimum of 30 minutes or until an administrator enables the user ID.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.1.8: 8.1.8 If a session has been idle for more than 15 minutes, require the user to re-authenticate to re-activate the terminal or session.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.2: 8.2 In addition to assigning a unique ID, ensure proper user-authentication management for non-consumer users and administrators on all system components by employing at least one of the following methods to authenticate all users:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.2.1: 8.2.1 Using strong cryptography, render all authentication credentials (such as passwords/phrases) unreadable during transmission and storage on all system components.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.2.2: 8.2.2 Verify user identity before modifying any authentication credential
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.2.4: 8.2.4 Change user passwords/passphrases at least once every 90 days.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.2.5: 8.2.5 Do not allow an individual to submit a new password/phrase that is the same as any of the last four passwords/phrases he or she has used.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.2.6: 8.2.6 Set passwords/phrases for first- time use and upon reset to a unique value for each user, and change immediately after the first use.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.3: 8.3 Incorporate two-factor authentication for remote network access originating from outside the network by personnel (including users and administrators) and all third parties, (including vendor access for support or maintenance). Note: Two-factor authentication requires that two of the three authentication methods (see Requirement 8.2 for descriptions of authentication methods) be used for authentication. Using one factor twice (for example, using two separate passwords) is not considered two-factor authentication.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.4: 8.4 Document and communicate authentication policies and procedures to all users including:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.5: 8.5 Do not use group, shared, or generic IDs, passwords, or other authentication methods as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.5.1: 8.5.1 Additional requirement for service providers only: Service providers with remote access to customer premises (for example, for support of POS systems or servers) must use a unique authentication credential (such as a password/phrase) for each customer.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.6: 8.6 Where other authentication mechanisms are used (for example, physical or logical security tokens, smart cards, certificates, etc.), use of these mechanisms must be assigned as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.7: 8.7 All access to any database containing cardholder data (including access by applications, administrators, and all other users) is restricted as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-8.8: 8.8 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for identification and authentication are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.1: 9.1 Use appropriate facility entry controls to limit and monitor physical access to systems in the cardholder data environment.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.1.1: 9.1.1 Use video cameras and/or access control mechanisms to monitor individual physical access to sensitive areas. Review collected data and correlate with other entries. Store for at least three months, unless otherwise restricted by law.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.1.2: 9.1.2 Implement physical and/or logical controls to restrict access to publicly accessible network jacks.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.1.3: 9.1.3 Restrict physical access to wireless access points, gateways, handheld devices, networking/communications hardware, and telecommunication lines.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.2: 9.2 Develop procedures to easily distinguish between onsite personnel and visitors
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.3: 9.3 Control physical access for onsite personnel to sensitive areas as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.4: 9.4 Implement procedures to identify and authorize visitors.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.4.1: 9.4.1 Visitors are authorized before entering, and escorted at all times within, areas where cardholder data is processed or maintained.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.4.2: 9.4.2 Visitors are identified and given a badge or other identification that expires and that visibly distinguishes the visitors from onsite personnel.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.4.3: 9.4.3 Visitors are asked to surrender the badge or identification before leaving the facility or at the date of expiration.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.4.4: 9.4.4 A visitor log is used to maintain a physical audit trail of visitor activity to the facility as well as computer rooms and data centers where cardholder data is stored or transmitted.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.5.1: 9.5.1 Store media backups in a secure location, preferably an off-site facility, such as an alternate or backup site, or a commercial storage facility. Review the location\u2019s security at least annually.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.6: 9.6 Maintain strict control over the internal or external distribution of any kind of media, including the following:'
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.6.1: 9.6.1 Classify media so the sensitivity of the data can be determined.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.6.2: 9.6.2 Send the media by secured courier or other delivery method that can be accurately tracked.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.6.3: 9.6.3 Ensure management approves any and all media that is moved from a secured area (including when media is distributed to individuals).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.7: 9.7 Maintain strict control over the storage and accessibility of media.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.7.1: 9.7.1 Properly maintain inventory logs of all media and conduct media inventories at least annually.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.8: 9.8 Destroy media when it is no longer needed for business or legal reasons as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.8.1: 9.8.1 Shred, incinerate, or pulp hard- copy materials so that cardholder data cannot be reconstructed. Secure storage containers used for materials that are to be destroyed.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.8.2: 9.8.2 Render cardholder data on electronic media unrecoverable so that cardholder data cannot be reconstructed.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.9: 9.9 Protect devices that capture payment card data via direct physical interaction with the card from tampering and substitution.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.9.1: 9.9.1 Maintain an up-to-date list of devices.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.9.2: 9.9.2 Periodically inspect device surfaces to detect tampering (for example, addition of card skimmers to devices), or substitution (for example, by checking the serial number or other device characteristics to verify it has not been swapped with a fraudulent device).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.9.3: 9.9.3 Provide training for personnel to be aware of attempted tampering or replacement of devices.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-9.10: 9.10 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for restricting physical access to cardholder data are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.1: 10.1 Implement audit trails to link all access to system components to each individual user.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.2: 10.2 Implement automated audit trails for all system components to reconstruct the following events:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.2.1: 10.2.1 All individual user accesses to cardholder data
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.2.2: 10.2.2 All actions taken by any individual with root or administrative privileges
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.2.5: 10.2.5 Use of and changes to identification and authentication mechanisms -- including but not limited to creation of new accounts and elevation of privileges -- and all changes, additions, or deletions to accounts with root or administrative privileges
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.2.6: 10.2.6 Initialization, stopping, or pausing of the audit logs
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.2.7: 10.2.7 Creation and deletion of system- level objects
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.3: 10.3 Record at least the following audit trail entries for all system components for each event:'
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.3.6: 10.3.6 Identity or name of affected data, system component, or resource.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.4: 10.4 Using time-synchronization technology, synchronize all critical system clocks and times and ensure that the following is implemented for acquiring, distributing, and storing time.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.4.1: 10.4.1 Critical systems have the correct and consistent time.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.4.3: 10.4.3 Time settings are received from industry-accepted time sources.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.5: 10.5 Secure audit trails so they cannot be altered.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.5.1: 10.5.1 Limit viewing of audit trails to those with a job-related need.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.5.2: 10.5.2 Protect audit trail files from unauthorized modifications.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.5.3: 10.5.3 Promptly back up audit trail files to a centralized log server or media that is difficult to alter.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.5.4: 10.5.4 Write logs for external-facing technologies onto a secure, centralized, internal log server or media device.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.5.5: 10.5.5 Use file-integrity monitoring or change-detection software on logs to ensure that existing log data cannot be changed without generating alerts (although new data being added should not cause an alert).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.6: 10.6 Review logs and security events for all system components to identify anomalies or suspicious activity.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.6.1: 10.6.1 Review the following at least daily:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.6.2: 10.6.2 Review logs of all other system components periodically based on the organization's policies and risk management strategy, as determined by the organization's annual risk assessment.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.6.3: 10.6.3 Follow up exceptions and anomalies identified during the review process.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.7: 10.7 Retain audit trail history for at least one year, with a minimum of three months immediately available for analysis (for example, online, archived, or restorable from backup).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-10.8: 10.8 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for monitoring all access to network resources and cardholder data are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.1: 11.1 Implement processes to test for the presence of wireless access points (802.11), and detect and identify all authorized and unauthorized wireless access points on a quarterly basis.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.1.1: 11.1.1 Maintain an inventory of authorized wireless access points including a documented business justification.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.1.2: 11.1.2 Implement incident response procedures in the event unauthorized wireless access points are detected.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.2: 11.2 Run internal and external network vulnerability scans at least quarterly and after any significant change in the network (such as new system component installations, changes in network topology, firewall rule modifications, product upgrades).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.2.1: 11.2.1 Perform quarterly internal vulnerability scans and rescans as needed, until all 'high-risk' vulnerabilities (as identified in Requirement 6.1) are resolved. Scans must be performed by qualified personnel.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.2.2: 11.2.2 Perform quarterly external vulnerability scans, via an Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV) approved by the Payment Card Industry Security Standards Council (PCI SSC). Perform rescans as needed, until passing scans are achieved.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.2.3: 11.2.3 Perform internal and external scans, and rescans as needed, after any significant change. Scans must be performed by qualified personnel.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.3: 11.3 Implement a methodology for penetration testing that includes the following:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.3.1: 11.3.1 Perform external penetration testing at least annually and after any significant infrastructure or application upgrade or modification (such as an operating system upgrade, a sub-network added to the environment, or a web server added to the environment).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.3.2: 11.3.2 Perform internal penetration testing at least annually and after any significant infrastructure or application upgrade or modification (such as an operating system upgrade, a sub-network added to the environment, or a web server added to the environment).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.3.3: 11.3.3 Exploitable vulnerabilities found during penetration testing are corrected and testing is repeated to verify the corrections.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.3.4: 11.3.4 If segmentation is used to isolate the CDE from other networks, perform penetration tests at least annually and after any changes to segmentation controls/methods to verify that the segmentation methods are operational and effective, and isolate all out-of-scope systems from systems in the CDE.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.4: 11.4 Use intrusion-detection and/or intrusion-prevention techniques to detect and/or prevent intrusions into the network. Monitor all traffic at the perimeter of the cardholder data environment as well as at critical points in the cardholder data environment, and alert personnel to suspected compromises.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.5: 11.5 Deploy a change-detection mechanism (for example, file-integrity monitoring tools) to alert personnel to unauthorized modification (including changes, additions, and deletions) of critical system files, configuration files, or content files; and configure the software to perform critical file comparisons at least weekly.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.5.1: 11.5.1 Implement a process to respond to any alerts generated by the change- detection solution.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-11.6: 11.6 Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for security monitoring and testing are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.1: 12.1 Establish, publish, maintain, and disseminate a security policy.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.1.1: 12.1.1 Review the security policy at least annually and update the policy when the environment changes.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.3: 12.3 Develop usage policies for critical technologies and define proper use of these technologies.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.3.2: 12.3.2 Authentication for use of the technology
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.3.3: 12.3.3 A list of all such devices and personnel with access
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.3.4: 12.3.4 A method to accurately and readily determine owner, contact information, and purpose (for example, labeling, coding, and/or inventorying of devices)
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.3.6: 12.3.6 Acceptable network locations for the technologies
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.3.8: 12.3.8 Automatic disconnect of sessions for remote-access technologies after a specific period of inactivity
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.3.9: 12.3.9 Activation of remote-access technologies for vendors and business partners only when needed by vendors and business partners, with immediate deactivation after use
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.3.10: 12.3.10 For personnel accessing cardholder data via remote-access technologies, prohibit the copying, moving, and storage of cardholder data onto local hard drives and removable electronic media, unless explicitly authorized for a defined business need.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.4: 12.4 Ensure that the security policy and procedures clearly define information security responsibilities for all personnel.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.5: 12.5 Assign to an individual or team the following information security management responsibilities:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.5.1: 12.5.1 Establish, document, and distribute security policies and procedures.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.5.2: 12.5.2 Monitor and analyze security alerts and information, and distribute to appropriate personnel.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.5.3: 12.5.3 Establish, document, and distribute security incident response and escalation procedures to ensure timely and effective handling of all situations.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.5.4: 12.5.4 Administer user accounts, including additions, deletions, and modifications.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.5.5: 12.5.5 Monitor and control all access to data.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.6: 12.6 Implement a formal security awareness program to make all personnel aware of the importance of cardholder data security.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.6.1: 12.6.1 Educate personnel upon hire and at least annually.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.6.2: 12.6.2 Require personnel to acknowledge at least annually that they have read and understood the security policy and procedures.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.7: 12.7 Screen potential personnel prior to hire to minimize the risk of attacks from internal sources. (Examples of background checks include previous employment history, criminal record, credit history, and reference checks.)
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.8: 12.8 Maintain and implement policies and procedures to manage service providers with whom cardholder data is shared, or that could affect the security of cardholder data, as follows:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.8.1: 12.8.1 Maintain a list of service providers.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.8.2: 12.8.2 Maintain a written agreement that includes an acknowledgement that the service providers are responsible for the security of cardholder data the service providers possess or otherwise store, process or transmit on behalf of the customer, or to the extent that they could impact the security of the customer's cardholder data environment.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.8.3: 12.8.3 Ensure there is an established process for engaging service providers including proper due diligence prior to engagement.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.8.4: 12.8.4 Maintain a program to monitor service providers' PCI DSS compliance status at least annually.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.8.5: 12.8.5 Maintain information about which PCI DSS requirements are managed by each service provider, and which are managed by the entity.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.9: 12.9 Additional requirement for service providers only: Service providers acknowledge in writing to customers that they are responsible for the security of cardholder data the service provider possesses or otherwise stores, processes, or transmits on behalf of the customer, or to the extent that they could impact the security of the customer's cardholder data environment.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.10: 12.10 Implement an incident response plan. Be prepared to respond immediately to a system breach.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.10.1: 12.10.1 Create the incident response plan to be implemented in the event of system breach. Ensure the plan addresses the following, at a minimum:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.10.2: 12.10.2 Test the plan at least annually.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.10.3: 12.10.3 Designate specific personnel to be available on a 24/7 basis to respond to alerts.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.10.4: 12.10.4 Provide appropriate training to staff with security breach response responsibilities.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.10.5: 12.10.5 Include alerts from security monitoring systems, including but not limited to intrusion-detection, intrusion- prevention, firewalls, and file-integrity monitoring systems.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-12.10.6: 12.10.6 Develop a process to modify and evolve the incident response plan according to lessons learned and to incorporate industry developments.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A.1: A.1 Protect each entity's (that is, merchant, service provider, or other entity) hosted environment and data, per A.1.1 through A.1.4:"
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A.1.1: A.1.1 Ensure that each entity only runs processes that have access to that entity's cardholder data environment.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A.1.2: A.1.2 Restrict each entity's access and privileges to its own cardholder data environment only.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A.1.3: A.1.3 Ensure logging and audit trails are enabled and unique to each entity's cardholder data environment and consistent with PCI DSS Requirement 10.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A.1.4: A.1.4 Enable processes to provide for timely forensic investigation in the event of a compromise to any hosted merchant or service provider.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.1.1: A3.1.1 Executive management shall establish responsibility for the protection of cardholder data and a PCI DSS compliance program to include:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.1.2: A3.1.2 A formal PCI DSS compliance program must be in place to include:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.1.3: A3.1.3 PCI DSS compliance roles and responsibilities must be specifically defined and formally assigned to one or more personnel, including at least the following:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.1.4: A3.1.4 Provide up-to-date PCI DSS and/or information security training at least annually to personnel with PCI DSS compliance responsibilities (as identified in A3.1.3).
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.1: A3.2.1 Document and confirm the accuracy of PCI DSS scope at least quarterly and upon significant changes to the in-scope environment. At a minimum, the quarterly scoping validation should include:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.2: A3.2.2 Determine PCI DSS scope impact for all changes to systems or networks, including additions of new systems and new network connections. Processes must include:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.2.1: A3.2.2.1 Upon completion of a change, all relevant PCI DSS requirements must be verified on all new or changed systems and networks, and documentation must be updated as applicable. Examples of PCI DSS requirements that should be verified include, but are not limited to:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.3: A3.2.3 Changes to organizational structure -- for example, a company merger or acquisition, change or reassignment of personnel with responsibility for security controls -- result in a formal (internal) review of the impact to PCI DSS scope and applicability of controls.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.4: A3.2.4 If segmentation is used, confirm PCI DSS scope by performing penetration testing on segmentation controls at least every six months and after any changes to segmentation controls/methods.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.5: A3.2.5 Implement a data-discovery methodology to confirm PCI DSS scope and to locate all sources and locations of clear- text PAN at least quarterly, and upon significant changes to the cardholder environment or processes.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.5.1: A3.2.5.1 Ensure effectiveness of methods used for data discovery—–e.g., methods must be able to discover clear-text PAN on all types of system components (for example, on each operating system or platform) and file formats in use.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.5.2: A3.2.5.2 Implement response procedures to be initiated upon the detection of clear- text PAN outside of the CDE to include:
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.6: A3.2.6 Implement mechanisms for detecting and preventing clear-text PAN from leaving the CDE via an unauthorized channel, method, or process, including generation of audit logs and alerts.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.2.6.1: A3.2.6.1 Implement response procedures to be initiated upon the detection of attempts to remove clear-text PAN from the CDE via an unauthorized channel, method, or process.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.3.1: A3.3.1 Implement a process to immediately detect and alert on critical security control failures.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.3.1.1: A3.3.1.1 Respond to failures of any critical security controls in a timely manner.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.3.2: A3.3.2 Review hardware and software technologies at least annually to confirm whether they continue to meet the organization's PCI DSS requirements.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.3.3: A3.3.3 Perform reviews at least quarterly to verify BAU activities are being followed.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.4.1: A3.4.1 Review user accounts and access privileges to in-scope system components at least every six months to ensure user accounts and access remain appropriate based on job function, and authorized.
controls.PCIDSS_3:Req-A3.5.1: A3.5.1 Implement a methodology for the timely identification of attack patterns and undesirable behavior across systems--for example, using coordinated manual reviews and/or centrally-managed or automated log correlation tools-- to include at least the following:
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.1: Processes and mechanisms for installing and maintaining network security controls are defined and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.1.1: All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 1 are Documented, Kept up to date, In use and Known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.1.2: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 1 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.2: Network Security Controls (NSCs) are configured and maintained.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.2.1: Configuration standards for NSC rulesets are Defined, Implemented and Maintained.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.2.2: All changes to network connections and to configurations of NSCs are approved and managed in accordance with the change control process defined at Requirement 6.5.1.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.2.3: An accurate network diagram(s) is maintained that shows all connections between the CDE and other networks, including any wireless networks.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.2.4: An accurate data-flow diagram(s) is maintained
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.2.5: All services, protocols, and ports allowed are identified, approved, and have a defined business need.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.2.6: Security features are defined and implemented for all services, protocols, and ports that are in use and considered to be insecure, such that the risk is mitigated.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.2.7: Configurations of NSCs are reviewed at least once every six months to confirm they are relevant and effective.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.2.8: Configuration files for NSCs are secured from unauthorized access and kept consistent with active network configurations.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.3: Network access to and from the cardholder data environment is restricted.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.3.1: Inbound traffic to the CDE is restricted to only traffic that is necessary
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.3.2: Outbound traffic from the CDE is restricted to only traffic that is necessary
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.3.3: NSCs are installed between all wireless networks and the CDE, regardless of whether the wireless network is a CDE.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.4: Network connections between trusted and untrusted networks are controlled.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.4.1: NSCs are implemented between trusted and untrusted networks.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.4.2: Inbound traffic from untrusted networks to trusted networks is restricted.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.4.3: Anti-spoofing measures are implemented to detect and block forged source IP addresses from entering the trusted network.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.4.4: System components that store cardholder data are not directly accessible from untrusted networks.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.4.5: The disclosure of internal IP addresses and routing information is limited to only authorized parties.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.5: Risks to the CDE from computing devices that are able to connect to both untrusted networks and the CDE are mitigated.
controls.PCIDSS_4:1.5.1: Security controls are implemented on any computing devices, including company- and employee-owned devices, that connect to both untrusted networks (including the Internet) and the CDE
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.1: Processes and mechanisms for applying secure configurations to all system components are defined and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.1.1: All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 2 are Documented, Kept up to date, In use and Known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.1.2: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 2 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.2: System components are configured and managed securely.
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.2.1: Configuration standards are developed, implemented, and maintained
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.2.3: Primary functions requiring different security levels are managed
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.2.4: Only necessary services, protocols, daemons, and functions are enabled, and all unnecessary functionality is removed or disabled
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.2.5: If any insecure services, protocols, or daemons are present, business justification is documented and the risk is reduced.
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.2.6: System security parameters are configured to prevent misuse.
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.2.7: All non-console administrative access is encrypted using strong cryptography.
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.3: Wireless environments are configured and managed securely.
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.3.1: For wireless environments connected to the CDE or transmitting account data, all wireless vendor defaults are changed at installation or are confirmed to be secure.
controls.PCIDSS_4:2.3.2: For wireless environments connected to the CDE or transmitting account data, wireless encryption keys are changed
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.1: Processes and mechanisms for protecting stored account data are defined and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.1.1: All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 3 are Documented, Kept up to date, In use and Known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.1.2: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 3 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.2: Storage of account data is kept to a minimum.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.2.1: Account data storage is kept to a minimum through implementation of data retention and disposal policies, procedures, and processes.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.3: Sensitive authentication data (SAD) is not stored after authorization.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.3.1: SAD is not stored after authorization, even if encrypted. All sensitive authentication data received is rendered unrecoverable upon completion of the authorization process.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.3.1.1: The full contents of any track are not stored upon completion of the authorization process.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.3.1.2: The card verification code is not stored upon completion of the authorization process.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.3.1.3: The personal identification number (PIN) and the PIN block are not stored upon completion of the authorization process.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.3.2: SAD that is stored electronically prior to completion of authorization is encrypted using strong cryptography.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.3.3: Additional requirement for issuers and companies that support issuing services and store sensitive authentication data.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.4: Access to displays of full PAN and ability to copy PAN is restricted.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.4.1: PAN is masked when displayed (the BIN and last four digits are the maximum number of digits to be displayed), such that only personnel with a legitimate business need can see more than the BIN and last four digits of the PAN.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.4.2: When using remote-access technologies, technical controls prevent copy and/or relocation of PAN for all personnel, except for those with documented, explicit authorization and a legitimate, defined business need.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.5: Primary account number (PAN) is secured wherever it is stored.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.5.1: PAN is rendered unreadable anywhere it is stored
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.5.1.1: Hashes used to render PAN unreadable (per the first bullet of Requirement 3.5.1) are keyed cryptographic hashes of the entire PAN, with associated key-management processes and procedures in accordance with Requirements 3.6 and 3.7.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.5.1.2: If disk-level or partition-level encryption (rather than file-, column-, or field-level database encryption) is used to render PAN unreadable, it is implemented only on removable electronic media or complemented by another mechanism that meets Requirement 3.5.1
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.5.1.3: If disk-level or partition-level encryption is used (rather than file-, column-, or field--level database encryption) to render PAN unreadable, it is managed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.6: Cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data are secured.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.6.1: Procedures are defined and implemented to protect cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data against disclosure and misuse.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.6.1.1: Additional requirement for service providers only: A documented description of the cryptographic architecture is maintained
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.6.1.2: Secret and private keys used to encrypt/decrypt stored account data are stored in secure forms.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.6.1.3: Access to cleartext cryptographic key components is restricted to the fewest number of custodians necessary.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.6.1.4: Cryptographic keys are stored in the fewest possible locations.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7: Where cryptography is used to protect stored account data, key management processes and procedures covering all aspects of the key lifecycle are defined and implemented.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7.1: Key-management policies and procedures are implemented to include generation of strong cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7.2: Key-management policies and procedures are implemented to include secure distribution of cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7.3: Key-management policies and procedures are implemented to include secure storage of cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7.4: Key management policies and procedures are implemented for cryptographic key changes for keys that have reached the end of their cryptoperiod, as defined by the associated application vendor or key owner, and based on industry best practices and guidelines.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7.5: Key management policies procedures are implemented to include the retirement, replacement, or destruction of keys used to protect stored account data, as deemed necessary.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7.6: Where manual cleartext cryptographic key-management operations are performed by personnel, key-management policies and procedures are implemented include managing these operations using split knowledge and dual control.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7.7: Key management policies and procedures are implemented to include the prevention of unauthorized substitution of cryptographic keys.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7.8: Key management policies and procedures are implemented to include that cryptographic key custodians formally acknowledge (in writing or electronically) that they understand and accept their key-custodian responsibilities.
controls.PCIDSS_4:3.7.9: Additional requirement for service providers only: Where a service provider shares cryptographic keys with its customers for transmission or storage of account data, guidance on secure transmission, storage and updating of such keys is documented and distributed to the service provider’s customers.
controls.PCIDSS_4:4.1: Processes and mechanisms for protecting cardholder data with strong cryptography during transmission over open, public networks are defined and documented.
controls.PCIDSS_4:4.1.1: All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 4 are Documented, Kept up to date, In use and Known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_4:4.1.2: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 4 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:4.2: PAN is protected with strong cryptography during transmission.
controls.PCIDSS_4:4.2.1: Strong cryptography and security protocols are implemented as follows to safeguard PAN during transmission over open, public networks.
controls.PCIDSS_4:4.2.1.1: An inventory of the entity's trusted keys and certificates used to protect PAN during transmission is maintained.
controls.PCIDSS_4:4.2.1.2: Wireless networks transmitting PAN or connected to the CDE use industry best practices to implement strong cryptography for authentication and transmission.
controls.PCIDSS_4:4.2.2: PAN is secured with strong cryptography whenever it is sent via end-user messaging technologies.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.1: Processes and mechanisms for protecting all systems and networks from malicious software are defined and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.1.1: All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 5 are Documented, Kept up to date, In use and Known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.1.2: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 5 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.2: Malicious software (malware) is prevented, or detected and addressed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.2.1: An anti-malware solution(s) is deployed on all system components, except for those system components identified in periodic evaluations per Requirement 5.2.3 that concludes the system components are not at risk from malware.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.2.2: The deployed anti-malware solution(s) detects all known types of malware and removes, blocks, or contains all known types of malware.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.2.3: Any system components that are not at risk for malware are evaluated periodically.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.2.3.1: The frequency of periodic evaluations of system components identified as not at risk for malware is defined in the entity's targeted risk analysis, which is performed according to all elements specified in Requirement 12.3.1.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.3: Anti-malware mechanisms and processes are active, maintained, and monitored.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.3.1: The anti-malware solution(s) is kept current via automatic updates.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.3.2: The anti-malware solution(s) performs periodic scans and active or real-time scans or performs continuous behavioral analysis of systems or processes.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.3.2.1: If periodic malware scans are performed to meet Requirement 5.3.2, the frequency of scans is defined in the entity's targeted risk analysis, which is performed according to all elements specified in Requirement 12.3.1.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.3.3: For removable electronic media, the anti-malware solution(s) performs automatic scans of when the media is inserted, connected, or logically mounted, or Performs continuous behavioral analysis of systems or processes when the media is inserted, connected, or logically mounted.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.3.4: Audit logs for the anti-malware solution(s) are enabled and retained in accordance with Requirement 10.5.1.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.3.5: Anti-malware mechanisms cannot be disabled or altered by users, unless specifically documented, and authorized by management on a case-by-case basis for a limited time period.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.4: Anti-phishing mechanisms protect users against phishing attacks.
controls.PCIDSS_4:5.4.1: Processes and automated mechanisms are in place to detect and protect personnel against phishing attacks.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.1: Processes and mechanisms for developing and maintaining secure systems and software are defined and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.1.1: All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 6 are Documented, Kept up to date, In use and Known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.1.2: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 6 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.2: Bespoke and custom software are developed securely.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.2.1: Bespoke and custom software are developed securely.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.2.2: Software development personnel working on bespoke and custom software are trained at least once every 12 months
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.2.3: Bespoke and custom software is reviewed prior to being released into production or to customers, to identify and correct potential coding vulnerabilities.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.2.3.1: If manual code reviews are performed for bespoke and custom software prior to release to production code changes co-reviewed and approved.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.2.4: Software engineering techniques or other methods are defined and in use by software development personnel to prevent or mitigate common software attacks and related vulnerabilities in bespoke and custom software.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.3: Security vulnerabilities are identified and addressed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.3.1: Security vulnerabilities are identified and managed
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.3.2: An inventory of bespoke and custom software, and third-party software components incorporated into bespoke and custom software is maintained to facilitate vulnerability and patch management.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.3.3: All system components are protected from known vulnerabilities by installing applicable security patches/updates.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.4: Public-facing web applications are protected against attacks.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.4.1: For public-facing web applications, new threats and vulnerabilities are addressed on an ongoing basis and these applications are protected against known attacks.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.4.2: For public-facing web applications, an automated technical solution is deployed that continually detects and prevents web-based attacks.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.4.3: All payment page scripts that are loaded and executed in the consumer's browser are managed
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.5: Changes to all system components are managed securely.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.5.1: Changes to all system components in the production environment are made according to established procedures.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.5.2: Upon completion of a significant change, all applicable PCI DSS requirements are confirmed to be in place on all new or changed systems and networks, and documentation is updated as applicable.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.5.3: Pre-production environments are separated from production environments and the separation is enforced with access controls.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.5.4: Roles and functions are separated between production and pre-production environments to provide accountability such that only reviewed and approved changes are deployed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.5.5: Live PANs are not used in pre-production environments, except where those environments are included in the CDE and protected in accordance with all applicable PCI DSS requirements.
controls.PCIDSS_4:6.5.6: Test data and test accounts are removed from system components before the system goes into production.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.1: Processes and mechanisms for restricting access to system components and cardholder data by business need to know are defined and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.1.1: All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 7 are Documented, Kept up to date, In use and Known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.1.2: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 7 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.2: Access to system components and data is appropriately defined and assigned.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.2.1: An access control model is defined and includes granting access
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.2.2: Access is assigned to users, including privileged users, based on job classification and function, and least privileges necessary to perform job responsibilities.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.2.3: Required privileges are approved by authorized personnel.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.2.4: All user accounts and related access privileges, including third-party/vendor accounts, are reviewed
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.2.5: All application and system accounts and related access privileges are assigned and managed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.2.5.1: All access by application and system accounts and related access privileges are reviewed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.2.6: All user access to query repositories of stored cardholder data is restricted
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.3: Access to system components and data is managed via an access control system(s).
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.3.1: An access control system(s) is in place that restricts access based on a user's need to know and covers all system components.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.3.2: The access control system(s) is configured to enforce permissions assigned to individuals, applications, and systems based on job classification and function.
controls.PCIDSS_4:7.3.3: The access control system(s) is set to "deny all" by default.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.1: Processes and mechanisms for identifying users and authenticating access to system components are defined and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.1.1: All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 8 are Documented, Kept up to date, In use and Known to all affected parties.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.1.2: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 8 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.2: User identification and related accounts for users and administrators are strictly managed throughout an account's lifecycle.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.2.1: All users are assigned a unique ID before access to system components or cardholder data is allowed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.2.2: Group, shared, or generic IDs, or other shared authentication credentials are only used when necessary on an exception basis, and are managed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.2.3: Additional requirement for service providers only: Service providers with remote access to customer premises use unique authentication factors for each customer premises.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.2.4: Addition, deletion, and modification of user IDs, authentication factors, and other identifier objects are managed
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.2.5: Access for terminated users is immediately revoked.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.2.6: Inactive user accounts are removed or disabled within 90 days of inactivity.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.2.7: Accounts used by third parties to access, support, or maintain system components via remote access are managed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.2.8: If a user session has been idle for more than 15 minutes, the user is required to re-authenticate to re-activate the terminal or session.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.3: Strong authentication for users and administrators is established and managed.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.3.1: All user access to system components for users and administrators is authenticated.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.3.2: Strong cryptography is used to render all authentication factors unreadable during transmission and storage on all system components.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.3.3: User identity is verified before modifying any authentication factor.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.3.5: If passwords/passphrases are used as authentication factors to meet Requirement 8.3.1, they are set and reset for each user.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.3.6: If passwords/passphrases are used as authentication factors to meet Requirement 8.3.1, they meet the minimum level of complexity.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.3.7: Individuals are not allowed to submit a new password/passphrase that is the same as any of the last four passwords/passphrases used.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.3.8: Authentication policies and procedures are documented and communicated to all users.
controls.PCIDSS_4:8.3.9: If passwords/passphrases are used as the only authentication factor for user access (i.e., in any single-factor authentication implementation) they should have a limited lifetime.
